subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance have its own opt-in timeout key and generic queue timeout callback, or should it reuse a host-owned existing compaction timeout/default contract?
rationale: Both directions can be technically safe, but they create different public configuration, plugin compatibility, and long-term queue API contracts that repository policy requires an owner to choose.

options.title: Use one existing timeout contract
options.body: Reuse or extend the existing compaction safety timeout unless a distinct operator requirement proves that deferred maintenance needs independent configuration.

options.title: Approve the opt-in contract
options.body: Keep this PR's separate disabled-by-default key and queue callback as the supported compatibility-preserving maintenance-abandonment API.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Leave maintenance unbounded for now and close or redesign the PR if maintainers do not want to own either timeout contract.

recommendation.title: Use one existing timeout contract
recommendation.body: Reuse or extend the existing compaction safety timeout unless a distinct operator requirement proves that deferred maintenance needs independent configuration.

likelyOwner.reason: The central product boundary is the pluggable context-engine maintenance lifecycle introduced in this person's merged history.
